description: Fix #9, discriminant-validity family 2: the narrative report cites the complete, correct evidence chain -- identical to 01_correct_answer_correct_evidence's citations, nothing missing, nothing fabricated -- but mule_network_findings.csv gets the network topology wrong: EXT401 (the real offshore exit point) is wrongly cleared, and N150 (an innocent, unrelated customer) is wrongly classified as the exit point instead. Perfect citation hygiene, wrong conclusion.
report_text: N100 sent funds to M201 (T1-001) and M202 (T1-002). Both forwarded to M301 (T1-003, T1-004), which sent funds offshore (T2-001).

claims.text: N100 sent funds to both first-layer mules.
Both first-layer mules forwarded funds to the aggregator.

flag: DISCRIMINANT VALIDITY (fix #9): EGHR (0.0, identical to 01) and evidence traceability (precision=1.0, recall=1.0, F1=1.0, identical to 01) score this fixture as PERFECT -- indistinguishable from the genuinely correct report. Only the structural findings.csv check catches the error: EXT401 (real exit point) wrongly cleared is a false negative, N150 (innocent) wrongly named exit point is a false positive. This is the sharpest possible case for why citing valid, gold-matching evidence correctly does not guarantee the conclusion drawn from it is correct. Pair with 09_correct_outcome_poor_traceability.json (the mirror-image failure) for the direct empirical demonstration that outcome correctness and evidence traceability are non-equivalent constructs. This upgrades 04_incorrect_conclusion_plausible_explanation.json (which asserts a wrong conclusion only in prose, unverifiable without a live LLM judge call) to a conclusion error that is objectively, mechanically checkable against real ground truth (N100/M201/M202/M301/EXT401's true roles), not merely asserted.
